items.name: Agent Harnesses & Coding-Agent Tooling
items.summary: Agent frameworks, harnesses, orchestration and cost control for coding agents; the runtime layer behind Claude Code workflows and multi-agent experiments.

items.name: Agent Skills & Knowledge Workspaces
items.summary: Skill libraries, curated skill lists and Claude Code skills for diagrams, second brains and content, feeding skill authoring and diagram tooling.

items.name: RAG, Memory & Document Intelligence
items.summary: Retrieval, memory, ontologies, LLM data processing, inference and ML models for building knowledge-grounded AI apps and pipelines.

items.name: SEC EDGAR & Finance Data
items.summary: EDGAR filing parsers, investing and open-data sources for financial exploration and analytics pipelines.

items.name: Django, ERP & Backend Web Apps
items.summary: Django ecosystem, ERP and business app frameworks, admin widgets, Postgres and deployment for the Python backend projects.

items.name: Jekyll Sites, Themes & Publishing
items.summary: Jekyll themes, GitHub Pages tooling, SEO, search and comments that power the zer0-mistakes family of sites.

items.name: Docs Platforms, Markdown & Diagramming
items.summary: Documentation generators, markdown editors, collaborative notes and diagram tools for knowledge bases and specs.

items.name: Frontend Frameworks & UI Libraries
items.summary: Web UI frameworks, component kits and small JS utilities for building front ends and dashboards.

items.name: Games, Retro Emulation & Creative Tools
items.summary: Pixel art, sprites, emulation, music and game tooling for the game and creative side projects.

items.name: Terminal, Shell & Dev Environment
items.summary: Shells, Linux setups, PowerShell profiles, containers, editor extensions and package managers for dev environment and CLI tooling.

AFK-surf/xnulinux.summary: An experimental loadable Linux kernel module that runs XNU to give arm64 Linux a macOS personality.
AFK-surf/xnulinux.why: A niche kernel-level compatibility layer. It has no real overlap with the fleet's Linux dotfiles or OS-dev projects and is far from their scope.

ideas: Borrow its source ingest and auto-linking skill flow
Apply its Karpathy-style LLM wiki structure to the knowledge base
AgriciDaniel/claude-obsidian.summary: Claude Code plugin that builds an Obsidian knowledge graph by reading, linking and filing sources into plain Markdown notes.
AgriciDaniel/claude-obsidian.why: LLM-maintained Markdown wiki matches the README knowledge-base project; its ingest and linking skills offer a pattern for the docs.

ideas: Reusable gate blocking TODOs and secrets in agent PRs
Commit-message hygiene check in shared workflows
Akimiya-z/codex-guard.summary: Quality-gate GitHub Action for AI-generated PRs that blocks TODO leftovers, leaked secrets, sloppy commits and failing CI.
Akimiya-z/codex-guard.why: Its checks for TODO leftovers, secrets and commit hygiene suit a shared reusable workflow guarding agent-authored PRs across every fleet repo.

AngelHuang5335/pantrykind.summary: A private, self-hosted Django kitchen companion that tracks food, suggests what to cook, and shares a shopping list.
AngelHuang5335/pantrykind.why: A small household pantry app with 53 stars; it has no overlap with the fleet's domains, and djangoerp's inventory needs are far larger.

ideas: Borrow its Dockerfile and settings layout for Django plus Postgres
Use its env-based DB configuration pattern
Azure-Samples/azure-django-postgres-flex.summary: Sample Django web app set up for deployment to Azure Container Apps with Azure PostgreSQL Flexible Server.
Azure-Samples/azure-django-postgres-flex.why: A reference for containerized Django plus Postgres deployment; the fleet has no Azure use, so only the structure is worth borrowing.

CameronFoxly/Ascii-Motion.summary: Web application for creating and animating ASCII art, built in TypeScript.
CameronFoxly/Ascii-Motion.why: Niche ASCII art editor; it doesn't map to any fleet project. bashcrawl is terminal-themed but needs no animation editor.

ideas: Try intent-based activation for zer0-CMS server-rendered admin pages
Use DOM morphing instead of a full JS framework for partial updates
CycleChain/CycleWire.summary: A zero-initial-JS engine that makes server-rendered HTML interactive on user intent, with DOM morphing and islands-style lazy activation.
CycleChain/CycleWire.why: Its Django and Rails support matches zer0-CMS's two planes, and intent-based hydration could add interactivity without a JS framework, but it is small and young at 57 stars.

Derpyu520/qq-bridge.summary: Bridge connecting QQ via OneBot v11 to DeepSeek Harness agents, with social simulation, safe MCP tools and slang learning.
Derpyu520/qq-bridge.why: It is a niche QQ-to-DeepSeek chat bridge tied to a platform and harness the fleet does not use.

ideas: Copy its profile, port, prove-equivalence skill structure
Study how it packages a Claude Code plugin with an MCP server
EL4CTEO/fast-anything.summary: A Claude Code plugin and MCP workflow that profiles Python, Node or Ruby apps, ports hot functions to Rust and checks behavior is unchanged.
EL4CTEO/fast-anything.why: It's an agent-skill and MCP package with a clear profile, port and verify loop. The skills project could borrow that structure for its own skills.

Ebony-Vinyl/EAC-Desktop.summary: Electron desktop app for running hundreds of DeepSeek Harness plugins side by side.
Ebony-Vinyl/EAC-Desktop.why: It is tied to the DeepSeek Harness plugin ecosystem, which the fleet does not use.

ideas: Publish zpl-viewer to Open VSX alongside the VS Code Marketplace
Add an ovsx publish step to the extension release workflow
EclipseFdn/open-vsx.org.summary: Source of the open-vsx.org website, a vendor-neutral registry and marketplace for VS Code extensions.
EclipseFdn/open-vsx.org.why: Open VSX is where VS Code extensions can be published for non-Microsoft editors; zpl-viewer and vs-sonic-pi could publish there, but the site source itself isn't needed.

FatelessAI/SkyrimNet-GamePlugin.summary: Skyrim mod that gives NPCs LLM-driven conversation, memory, actions and real-time text-to-speech voices.
FatelessAI/SkyrimNet-GamePlugin.why: A game mod in Papyrus for Skyrim with no overlap with any fleet project's stack or goals.

ideas: Borrow its lesson progression for godotgo onboarding
Reference it as learning material in godotgo docs
GDQuest/learn-gdscript.summary: Interactive in-browser course that teaches Godot's GDScript from zero, free and built with Godot.
GDQuest/learn-gdscript.why: Strong GDScript teaching content and a model for in-engine interactive lessons, though its license is 'other' so reuse needs checking.

ideas: Check which filing types and index endpoints it queries
Reuse its approach to parsing filing indexes
Gunratan/edgar.summary: An R tool for retrieving and parsing U.S. SEC EDGAR corporate filings.
Gunratan/edgar.why: Covers the same EDGAR filing retrieval domain, but it is in R, unlicensed and stale, so only its approach to filing parsing is worth borrowing.

ideas: Wrap different agent harnesses behind one session/streaming API
Adopt its conformance tests to benchmark harness behaviour in outbox
HarnessRouter/harnessrouter.summary: Self-hosted Apache-2.0 unified API for running agent harnesses like Codex and Claude Code, with sessions, streaming and conformance testing.
HarnessRouter/harnessrouter.why: Outbox benchmarks multi-agent systems; a unified harness API and conformance suite give a pattern for comparing different agent harnesses uniformly.

ideas: Natural-language transaction entry for djangoerp journal entries
Harvey-cream/accountings.summary: Chinese-language personal finance platform with bookkeeping, budgets and invoices, plus NL entry, RAG and CrewAI agent workflows on Django and uniapp.
Harvey-cream/accountings.why: Consumer personal-finance app with no license; overlaps djangoerp and law-ai only by stack, offering little reusable beyond the NL bookkeeping idea.

Hugo-Dz/spritefusion-sprite-normals.summary: Rust tool that generates normal maps from sprites and animated sprite sheets.
Hugo-Dz/spritefusion-sprite-normals.why: Pixel-art normal map generation has no clear fit; fleet game projects are an emulator and a Godot framework, not sprite-lighting pipelines.

ideas: Study its techniques for cutting LLM turns and tokens in MCP tools
INK-Q/agy-fast.summary: An MCP accelerator plugin for Google Antigravity that cuts LLM turns, token use and upload traffic.
INK-Q/agy-fast.why: Its MCP plugin approach to reducing tokens is interesting, but it targets Antigravity, which the fleet doesn't use. The performance figures are self-reported.

Immortal-Protocols/lastbook.summary: Offline knowledge AI with maps and videos intended for survival and rebuilding scenarios.
Immortal-Protocols/lastbook.why: Survival-focused offline knowledge app with no topics and no overlap with any fleet project's domain.

ideas: Model skills as a staged pipeline with handoffs between skills
Add a test-for-bugs skill stage after generation
Package a skill set under one repo with a shared convention
Jakeschincariol/replica-skill.summary: Eleven Claude skills that reverse-engineer an app, rebuild it, test it for bugs and fix what its users complain about.
Jakeschincariol/replica-skill.why: A well-structured multi-stage skill pipeline (analyze, rebuild, test, fix) shows how to chain agent skills; the app-cloning purpose itself isn't a fleet need.

ideas: Compare its cost-control tactics for PR review runs
Reuse its CLI mode to run reviews locally
Juror-AI/juror.summary: TypeScript CLI and GitHub Action for AI code review that runs on your own Actions, pitched as a cheaper Greptile alternative.
Juror-AI/juror.why: Another Actions-native AI PR reviewer in TypeScript; githubai already reviews PRs, so take its cost-saving design ideas instead of replacing anything.

Lemxy/WinRust.summary: A Windows shell replacement written in Rust, with a taskbar, file manager, NTFS search, task manager and disk cleaner in one installer.
Lemxy/WinRust.why: A Windows-only desktop shell, and the fleet has no Windows targets. The shared Rust language isn't enough reason to use it.

ideas: Review its EDGAR index and filing download logic
Borrow its approach to parsing filing metadata
LexPredict/openedgar.summary: OpenEDGAR, a Python toolkit for downloading and processing SEC EDGAR filings.
LexPredict/openedgar.why: It targets the same SEC EDGAR domain as edgar-pipeline and fredgar-ai. It's stale since 2022, so borrow its filing ingestion patterns instead of using it.

LukeSmithxyz/md-website-cv.summary: A system that builds personal websites and CVs/resumes from markdown files, last updated in 2020.
LukeSmithxyz/md-website-cv.why: Stale since 2020 and no license. The fleet already has Jekyll-based markdown resume and portfolio sites, so it adds little.

ideas: Add a persistent memory MCP server pattern to agent skills
Compare its recall approach against the fleet's markdown memory
MemPalace/mempalace.summary: Open-source AI memory system built on ChromaDB with MCP support, claiming top benchmark results.
MemPalace/mempalace.why: An MCP-exposed memory layer for agents fits the skills/MCP work; the benchmark claims are unverified here, so borrow patterns rather than adopt wholesale.

ideas: Add feature flags for staged rollout of fredgar-ai features
PostHog/posthog.summary: Product analytics platform with session replay, feature flags, experiments, error tracking and AI observability.
PostHog/posthog.why: Self-hostable analytics and feature flags could instrument fredgar-ai later, but nothing in the fleet needs product analytics yet.

PostHog/posthog.com.summary: Source of PostHog's official docs site, website and public handbook, built with Gatsby and Tailwind.
PostHog/posthog.com.why: A company-specific Gatsby site; the fleet's docs sites run on Jekyll, so little of it transfers directly.

ideas: Reuse its skill layout and prompt structure
Produce HTML explainers with embedded diagrams
Apply its writing-style constraints (ST E100) to skill output
QingYunA/answer-me-with-html.summary: An agent skill that has AI agents answer complex questions with a readable one-page HTML explainer.
QingYunA/answer-me-with-html.why: It is a compact example of a Claude Code skill that produces HTML explainers. The skill structure and its output conventions are worth borrowing.

ideas: Study its reporting engine design for ERP reports
Borrow its dashboard widget system
Look at its custom admin site structure
RamezIssac/django-erp-framework.summary: Django framework for building business apps, with a reporting engine, charts, widgets and a custom admin site.
RamezIssac/django-erp-framework.why: Directly overlaps djangoerp's Django and ERP domain; its reporting engine and widgets are worth borrowing, but AGPL licensing argues against adopting it wholesale.

ideas: Borrow its per-emulator module layout for core configs
Use its supported-systems list to plan platform coverage
RetroPie/RetroPie-Setup.summary: Shell script that sets up a Raspberry Pi, Odroid or PC with RetroArch emulator and various cores.
RetroPie/RetroPie-Setup.why: Mature emulation setup tooling with a core-module installer design; rewind-arcade can borrow its emulator catalog and per-system configuration approach.

ideas: Run a GEO and SEO audit skill against the site
Pull Search Console data through MCP for content decisions
Ryze-AI-Adgent/open-seo-mcp-skills.summary: Free SEO MCP server and Claude skills for keyword research, rank tracking, audits, backlinks and AI visibility using GSC, GA4 and ads data.
Ryze-AI-Adgent/open-seo-mcp-skills.why: SEO and GEO skills could help the Jekyll content sites rank, but it's a hosted third-party MCP backed by DataForSEO. Worth revisiting if SEO becomes a priority.

Shopify/hydrogen.summary: Shopify's framework of commerce primitives for building storefronts with React, Remix and Next.js.
Shopify/hydrogen.why: It is tied to Shopify storefronts and the fleet has no commerce project. The React overlap with cv-pro is too thin to matter.

ideas: Use its strict-mode and error-handling behaviours to harden theme templates
Follow its changelog for Liquid changes that affect Jekyll sites
Shopify/liquid.summary: Liquid template language in Ruby, a safe customer-facing templating engine for web apps.
Shopify/liquid.why: Jekyll uses Liquid, so knowing its internals helps the Jekyll theme; the project already depends on it indirectly through Jekyll.

SplashtopInc/winstall.summary: A web app for browsing winget packages and building an install command or script for Windows apps.
SplashtopInc/winstall.why: Windows-specific package browsing app with no overlap with the fleet's projects; GPL-3.0 licensing also limits reuse.

ideas: Copy the slim Alpine Jekyll Dockerfile approach for the dev container
Starefossen/docker-github-pages.summary: Alpine Docker image for building and serving GitHub Pages and Jekyll sites locally.
Starefossen/docker-github-pages.why: It matches the Jekyll and Docker dev setup, but it hasn't been updated since 2020. Borrow the Alpine Dockerfile pattern rather than depend on the image.

ideas: Copy its slash-command layout for research, write and optimize steps
Add an SEO analysis pass to the blog skill before publishing
TheCraigHewitt/seomachine.summary: Claude Code workspace with commands and agents for researching, writing, analyzing and optimizing long-form SEO blog content.
TheCraigHewitt/seomachine.why: Its Claude Code workflow for blog research and SEO analysis could inform the fleet's blog skill and content sites like lifehacker.dev.

TsekNet/PowerShell-Profile.why: A small, personal PowerShell profile last updated in 2021, with no relevance to the fleet.

ideas: Prototype tree-index retrieval alongside Qdrant for long documents
Compare reasoning-based retrieval against vector search on the same corpus
VectifyAI/PageIndex.summary: Document indexing for vectorless, reasoning-based RAG that retrieves via an LLM-navigated document structure instead of embeddings.
VectifyAI/PageIndex.why: ragio-ai uses Qdrant vector RAG; PageIndex's tree-index reasoning retrieval is a complementary approach for long structured documents like filings or legal texts.

ideas: Mine it for skills worth adding or adapting
Check skills against its cross-tool compatibility
Submit the fleet's own skills for listing
VoltAgent/awesome-agent-skills.summary: A curated list of more than 1000 agent skills from official teams and the community, for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and Cursor.
VoltAgent/awesome-agent-skills.why: It is a large, active index of agent skills across tools. It works as a discovery source and a benchmark for the skills repo.

ideas: Study its agent and tool abstractions for the skills SDK
Borrow its MCP integration patterns
Look at its observability approach for agent runs
VoltAgent/voltagent.summary: Open-source TypeScript framework and platform for building, running and observing AI agents with MCP support.
VoltAgent/voltagent.why: TypeScript agent framework with MCP overlaps the skills project's agents/MCP/SDK focus; useful as a reference for agent and tool abstractions rather than a dependency.

WayneChou-bot/WareTwin.summary: Real-time 3D digital twin of an autonomous warehouse with 20 AMRs, simulation, fleet scheduling, failure injection, VLM perception and an AI ops copilot.
WayneChou-bot/WareTwin.why: Warehouse robotics simulation; no fleet project works on robotics or logistics. The 'amr' topic means mobile robots here, not the developer's handle.

ideas: Try it to map cross-repo structure in the dash monorepo
abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus.summary: A zero-server code intelligence engine for analyzing codebases, with no description or topics beyond the tagline.
abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus.why: Code intelligence across repos could help the dash monorepo with many submodules, but the data gives few details, so evaluate before committing.

ideas: Borrow its CV and publications collection layout
Reuse its author sidebar profile pattern
academicpages/academicpages.github.io.summary: GitHub Pages Jekyll template for personal and academic portfolio websites written in HTML and Markdown.
academicpages/academicpages.github.io.why: Its portfolio page structure for CV, publications and talks maps onto the personal portfolio site, without needing a full switch.

ideas: Trial it for rich-text notes fields in the Django admin
Review its widget approach for Markdown preview in forms
agusmakmun/django-markdown-editor.summary: A Django Markdown editor widget supporting Bootstrap, Semantic UI and Tailwind, with live preview and editor features.
agusmakmun/django-markdown-editor.why: It could give ERP notes and description fields Markdown editing, but its GPL-3.0 license may conflict with fleet licensing, so check before use.

ideas: Add an optional DocSearch widget to the Jekyll theme
Evaluate its crawler config for the it-journey docs site
algolia/docsearch.summary: Algolia DocSearch adds a search box to documentation sites, with JavaScript, React and TypeScript components.
algolia/docsearch.why: Actively maintained. It could provide search for the Jekyll theme and documentation sites. It needs an Algolia index, so it is a borrow rather than a full adopt.

ideas: Borrow its InstantSearch front-end wiring for the theme
algolia/jekyll-algolia-example.summary: Front-end example site demonstrating the jekyll-algolia search plugin.
algolia/jekyll-algolia-example.why: Shows how to wire Algolia search into a Jekyll front end; zer0-mistakes theme could borrow the search UI pattern, though the example is old and unlicensed.

ideas: Borrow its publications and CV page layouts for the portfolio
Review its dark mode toggle implementation
Take its GitHub Pages deploy workflow as a reference
alshedivat/al-folio.summary: A clean, responsive Jekyll theme for academics, covering portfolio, blog and personal sites on GitHub Pages.
alshedivat/al-folio.why: Popular, maintained Jekyll portfolio theme. Its layout and GitHub Pages setup can inform the portfolio site without replacing the zer0-mistakes theme.

ideas: Evaluate its offline-first sync model for sensor data
amark/gun.summary: A decentralized, offline-first graph database and sync protocol in JavaScript.
amark/gun.why: Offline-first peer-to-peer sync is interesting for IoT data, but the fleet has no clear need and its security claims need scrutiny.

ideas: Feed alert context to an LLM for root-cause suggestions
anakhas771/AI-Incident-Response-Platform.summary: AI-powered SRE platform that detects and investigates production incidents with RAG root-cause analysis and recommendations, on Django, Celery and Docker.
anakhas771/AI-Incident-Response-Platform.why: Incident RCA with RAG could sit on top of the fleet's Prometheus/OTel stack, but it is young and has an unclear 'other' license.

angular/angular.summary: Google's TypeScript web application framework for building performant, scalable web apps with PWA support.
angular/angular.why: The fleet's front ends use React, Vite, Jekyll and Compose; adopting Angular would add a heavy framework with no matching project.

ideas: Consider its data table and form components for the SEC filings UI
ant-design/ant-design.summary: Enterprise-class React UI component library and design language in TypeScript.
ant-design/ant-design.why: A mature React component set that could speed up fredgar-ai's frontend, but adopting it is a heavy styling commitment not yet needed.

ideas: Align SKILL.md frontmatter and layout with the official spec
Port useful reference skills into the fleet's skills repo
Use its skill-creator pattern to validate new skills
anthropics/skills.summary: Anthropic's official public repository of Agent Skills, with reference skill implementations and the skill format used by Claude.
anthropics/skills.why: Canonical source for the Agent Skills format and examples; the skills project should follow its structure and conventions directly.

ideas: Try it as a Docker Desktop alternative for running local observability containers
apple/container.summary: Swift tool for creating and running Linux containers as lightweight VMs on Apple silicon Macs.
apple/container.why: Could replace Docker Desktop for local docker-compose-style stacks on a Mac, but it's a different runtime and compose compatibility is unclear from the data.

ideas: Standardize README badges in the .github template repo
Use badge-maker to generate custom fleet status badges
badges/shields.summary: A service and library that generates consistent SVG and raster status badges, with badge-maker for custom ones.
badges/shields.why: Active and widely used. Its badges suit READMEs and CI status across the fleet, and the .github repo can standardize them in templates.

ideas: Define JSON Schemas for custom-field data on ERP records
Reuse its schema-driven form idea for SCHEMA-style validation
bhch/django-jsonform.summary: A Django admin form field for editing JSON data through a schema-driven UI, with Postgres ArrayField support.
bhch/django-jsonform.why: Schema-validated JSON editing suits flexible ERP fields, but the last push was January 2025, so check maintenance and Django compatibility first.

bmorelli25/Become-A-Full-Stack-Web-Devel.summary: A free list of resources for learning full-stack web development.
bmorelli25/Become-A-Full-Stack-Web-Devel.why: Generic beginner resource list, not updated since 2024. It might loosely inform learning-path content, but it has no concrete use for the fleet.

busy-app/busybar-firmware.summary: Firmware source code for the BUSY Bar device, written in C.
busy-app/busybar-firmware.why: Product-specific firmware with a non-standard license and no description or topics; little transferable beyond generic embedded C structure.

ideas: Study its subagent delegation and long-horizon task decomposition
Borrow the sandboxed execution pattern for benchmark runs
Adopt its memory layer design for persistent agent context
bytedance/deer-flow.summary: Open-source long-horizon SuperAgent harness using sandboxes, memory, tools, skills and subagents to research, code and create.
bytedance/deer-flow.why: A multi-agent harness with sandboxes, memory and subagents overlaps outbox's multi-agent research focus; worth mining its architecture rather than adopting wholesale.

ideas: Add official tech logos to generated architecture diagrams
Copy its one-sentence-to-diagram skill prompt design
caru-ini/stack-diagram.summary: Agent skill that turns a one-sentence stack description into an architecture diagram using official technology logos.
caru-ini/stack-diagram.why: Closely matches archify's diagram-agent scope; its official-logo approach and skill packaging are worth borrowing.

ideas: Study its phone-to-computer remote control flow for fleet-mobile
Review how it presents agent sessions in a mobile UI
ccch1mneyyy/dsh-Go.summary: Flutter/Android app that runs the DeepSeek Harness coding agent locally on a phone and can remotely control a computer.
ccch1mneyyy/dsh-Go.why: Mobile monitoring and remote control of agents parallels fleet-mobile's goal, but it is DeepSeek-specific, Flutter-based and AGPL-licensed, so it fits only as a reference.

ideas: Copy the Docker Compose layout for Dagster with dbt and DuckDB
Wire dbt models into Dagster assets
Add a Superset layer for BI dashboards
cnstlungu/portable-data-stack-dagster.summary: A portable datamart and BI stack built with Docker, Dagster, dbt, DuckDB and Superset.
cnstlungu/portable-data-stack-dagster.why: Its stack overlaps strongly with edgar-pipeline (Dagster, dbt, DuckDB). It is a good reference for Docker packaging and for how the layers connect.

ideas: Borrow its PWA offline support setup
Copy its devcontainer config for contributors
Take its table-of-contents and dark mode patterns
cotes2020/jekyll-theme-chirpy.summary: Minimal, responsive, feature-rich Jekyll theme for technical writing, packaged as a gem with PWA support.
cotes2020/jekyll-theme-chirpy.why: Actively maintained Bootstrap-adjacent Jekyll theme with gem packaging, PWA and devcontainer; zer0-mistakes can borrow features and structure.

counsyl/stor.summary: Cross-compatible CLI and Python API for accessing block and object storage.
counsyl/stor.why: Generic storage abstraction with little stated relevance to ocrmd or other fleet projects, and its license is non-standard.

databluedev/searchmirror.summary: Self-hosted rank tracker and AI-visibility monitor on the DataBlue SERP API, built with Django and React and licensed AGPL-3.0.
databluedev/searchmirror.why: Depends on a paid third-party SERP API and the AGPL license is a poor fit for the fleet; no fleet project does rank tracking.

ideas: Render QR previews for ZPL label fields
davidshimjs/qrcodejs.summary: Cross-browser JavaScript library that generates QR codes.
davidshimjs/qrcodejs.why: QR rendering could preview barcode or QR elements in label output, but the library has had no push since 2024 and the ZPL viewer may need ZPL-specific rendering.

ideas: Use it as the ingestion source for filings and XBRL financials
Feed its parsed financials into dbt and DuckDB models
Reuse it in fredgar-ai for SEC data access
dgunning/edgartools.summary: Python library for reading and analyzing SEC EDGAR filings, including 10-K, 8-K, XBRL financials, Form 3/4/5 and 13F.
dgunning/edgartools.why: A well-typed, MIT-licensed, actively maintained EDGAR client that can replace hand-rolled filing fetch and XBRL parsing in the pipeline; also relevant to fredgar-ai.

ideas: Bundle Dialogic as the default dialogue addon in godotgo templates
Use its character and timeline resources as a model for the framework's data format
dialogic-godot/dialogic.summary: A Godot addon for building dialogues, visual novels, RPGs and character management in GDScript.
dialogic-godot/dialogic.why: It's an actively maintained, MIT-licensed Godot dialogue plugin. godotgo is a Godot game framework and could use it directly for dialogue and characters.

discourse/discourse.summary: Large open source Ruby on Rails and Ember forum and community discussion platform.
discourse/discourse.why: A full forum platform that is heavy to run. The fleet's Rails and Jekyll projects only need a few patterns and have no community forum requirement.

ideas: Study its placeholder and plugin model for page composition
Borrow its frontend inline editing workflow ideas
django-cms/django-cms.summary: An enterprise CMS built on Django, with a developer-friendly structure and a content editing interface.
django-cms/django-cms.why: zer0-CMS is a Rails/Jekyll/Wagtail CMS fork; django-cms offers a comparable CMS model whose plugin and placeholder patterns are worth studying.

ideas: Add admin import/export for chart of accounts and journal entries
Use dry-run import to validate data before committing
Export ledger reports to CSV/XLSX from the admin
django-import-export/django-import-expor.summary: A Django app and library for importing and exporting data in CSV, XLS, JSON and other formats, with admin integration.
django-import-export/django-import-expor.why: An accounting ERP needs bulk loading of ledgers, charts of accounts and invoices; this gives admin-integrated import and export with dry-run previews.

ideas: Keep djangoerp on the current LTS release and track its deprecations
Use database constraints and transactions for ledger integrity
Share a common settings and app layout across the Django projects
django/django.summary: The widely used Python web framework with ORM, templates, views and an admin, for building web apps quickly.
django/django.why: Django is already the base of several fleet projects, and djangoerp is the one that most depends on its ORM, admin and migrations for an accounting system.

ideas: Add as a reusable preflight workflow before going public
Wrap into scripts' repo-management Bash utilities
duy90utc528/repo-publication-audit.summary: Dependency-free Python preflight checks, usable as a GitHub Action, that scan a repository for secrets and issues before making it public.
duy90utc528/repo-publication-audit.why: A zero-dependency pre-publication audit fits as a shared reusable workflow for the many fleet repos that get flipped public, with MIT licensing.

ideas: Define sensor nodes with declarative YAML configs
Borrow its component and platform abstraction
Add OTA update and MQTT discovery conventions
esphome/esphome.summary: A system that configures ESP32, ESP8266 and RP2040 devices from YAML files and connects them to home automation systems and MQTT.
esphome/esphome.why: It covers the same ground as sensor-mesh (ESP32, MQTT, PlatformIO). Its YAML-driven device config and component model are worth borrowing.

ideas: Define content types and front matter schemas to drive editing forms
Add a content dashboard listing drafts and published pages
Use a VS Code webview panel for a CMS UI
estruyf/vscode-front-matter.summary: A VS Code extension that works as a CMS for Markdown content in static site generators such as Jekyll, Hugo and Next.js.
estruyf/vscode-front-matter.why: It is a mature in-editor CMS for Markdown and Jekyll content. zer0-CMS can borrow its content-model and editor UX ideas without adopting the whole extension.

ether/etherpad.summary: Modern realtime collaborative document editor with a plugin framework, self-hostable.
ether/etherpad.why: A realtime collaborative editor server does not match any fleet project's needs, since the fleet's content workflows are git-based.

ideas: Export archify diagrams as .excalidraw JSON scenes
